title: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation
outcomes: Price forwards and futures and use them to hedge.
Value options using binomial, risk-neutral and Black-Scholes methods.
Explain credit, commodity and real options.

meta.exam_tip: Always state whether rates are continuous or discrete before pricing.

concepts.title: Forwards and futures: features and pricing
body: A derivative's value comes from an underlying asset. Forwards are private, customised agreements to buy or sell later at a fixed price, with counterparty risk and settlement at maturity. Futures are standardised, exchange-traded, cleared through a clearing house, margined and marked to market daily.

Cost-of-carry pricing: F = S × e^(rt) with continuous compounding (or S(1 + r)^t discretely); deduct the present value of dividends or add storage costs as relevant. If the market futures price is above fair value, sell futures and buy spot (cash-and-carry arbitrage); if below, the reverse.
Index futures let investors hedge or take market views cheaply; hedging a portfolio needs number of contracts = portfolio value × beta ÷ value of one futures contract.
concepts.analogy: Futures price = spot carried forward at the financing cost.
concepts.work: A ₹220 share with 8% carry for 3 months has a futures price near ₹224.44.

concepts.title: Options: types and pay-offs
body: An option gives the buyer the right, not obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) at a strike price; the writer receives a premium and bears the obligation. European options exercise only at expiry; American options at any time up to expiry.
Pay-offs at expiry: long call = max(S − K, 0) − premium; short call is the mirror; long put = max(K − S, 0) − premium; short put is the mirror. Options can be in, at or out of the money.
Compared with futures, options limit the buyer's loss to the premium while keeping upside, at the cost of paying that premium.
concepts.analogy: Buyers pay for rights; writers are paid to take obligations.
concepts.work: A call with strike ₹105 is worthless at expiry if the share ends at ₹90.

concepts.title: Option valuation: binomial, risk-neutral and Black-Scholes
body: Binomial model: the share moves up or down each period; build a riskless hedge or use risk-neutral probability p = (1 + r − d) ÷ (u − d), value = expected pay-off under p discounted at the risk-free rate. Multi-period trees work backwards.

Black-Scholes (European, non-dividend): C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rt)·N(d₂), with d₁ = [ln(S/K) + (r + σ²/2)t] ÷ (σ√t) and d₂ = d₁ − σ√t. Assumptions: lognormal prices, constant volatility and rate, no transaction costs, continuous trading.
Put-call parity: C + K·e^(−rt) = P + S (or with discrete discounting). Deviations create arbitrage.
concepts.analogy: Value options as if investors were risk-neutral, then discount at the risk-free rate.
concepts.work: With equal up and down probabilities, the call worth ₹15 in the up state is worth ₹7.14 today.

concepts.title: Greeks and exotic options
body: Factors raising call value: higher share price, lower strike, longer time, higher volatility, higher interest rates, lower dividends (puts mostly reverse).
Greeks: delta (change in option price per ₹1 change in share price; hedge ratio), gamma (change in delta), theta (time decay), rho (sensitivity to interest rate) and vega (sensitivity to volatility).
Exotic options have non-standard features: Asian (average price), barrier (knock-in/out), binary (fixed payout), lookback (best price over life), basket and compound options.
concepts.analogy: Greeks tell traders how options react to each driver.
concepts.work: A delta of 0.6 means the call gains about 60 paise when the share rises ₹1.

concepts.title: Credit, commodity and real options
body: Credit derivatives transfer credit risk: credit default swaps (protection buyer pays a spread; seller pays on a credit event, settled physically or in cash) and collateralised debt obligations (pools of debt sliced into tranches — risky when underlying quality is poor).

Commodity derivatives hedge prices of metals, energy and agricultural goods; weather and electricity derivatives hedge volume and price risks linked to temperature, rainfall or power demand. Past derivative mishaps show the dangers of leverage, poor controls and model risk.
Real options are flexibility in real projects — options to expand, abandon, delay or switch — valued with option models; they can make a project worth more than its static NPV.
concepts.analogy: Derivatives can move credit, commodity and even project flexibility risk.
concepts.work: An option to abandon a mine if prices crash has real value.

illustrations.title: Futures and a one-step binomial
illustrations.q: (a) A share trades at ₹220; the continuously compounded risk-free rate is 8% a year; no dividends. Price a 3-month future. (b) Another share is at ₹100 and can go to ₹120 or ₹90 in one period; the risk-free rate per period is 5%. Value a European call with strike ₹105 and the matching put.

illustrations.title: Black-Scholes call
illustrations.q: S = ₹100, K = ₹100, time 1 year, continuously compounded risk-free rate 10%, volatility 20%. Given d₁ = 0.60 and d₂ = 0.40, N(0.60) = 0.7257 and N(0.40) = 0.6554, compute the call value. Show how d₁ is derived.

jobs.title: Hedging a portfolio with derivatives
jobs.situation: A fund worries about a market fall over the next month.
steps: Compute futures contracts needed using beta.
Check fair value and arbitrage gaps.

mcqs.q: Futures differ from forwards in being:
options: Standardised and exchange-traded with daily margining
mcqs.explain: Clearing house reduces counterparty risk. In practice: mark to market.
mcqs.topic: Forwards and futures: features and pricing

mcqs.q: Under cost of carry with continuous compounding, F equals:
mcqs.explain: Financing cost added. In practice: deduct dividends.
mcqs.topic: Forwards and futures: features and pricing

mcqs.q: The maximum loss to a call buyer is:
mcqs.explain: Right, not obligation. In practice: writer faces large loss.

mcqs.q: Risk-neutral probability of an up move equals:
mcqs.explain: Binomial model. In practice: discount at risk-free.
mcqs.topic: Option valuation: binomial, risk-neutral and Black-Scholes

mcqs.explain: Arbitrage relation. In practice: European options.
mcqs.topic: Option valuation: binomial, risk-neutral and Black-Scholes

mcqs.explain: Options lose value with time. In practice: writers benefit.

mcqs.q: Higher volatility generally makes a call option:
mcqs.explain: Greater upside chance. In practice: vega positive.

mcqs.q: A credit default swap protection seller:
options: Receives a spread and pays on a credit event
mcqs.explain: Insurance-like. In practice: settlement physical or cash.

summary: Hedge contracts = value × β ÷ contract value.
Greeks: delta, gamma, theta, rho, vega.
remember: Put-call parity links calls and puts.
traps: Discounting option pay-offs at the expected return.

viva.model: Daily settlement of gains and losses on futures positions through the margin account based on closing prices.
European options can be exercised only at expiry; American options at any time up to expiry.
Call value equals share price times N of d1 minus the discounted strike times N of d2.
The change in option value for a one-unit change in the underlying price, used as the hedge ratio.

viva.model: Options to expand, to abandon and to delay or wait.

cases.title: Nova Capital desk
cases.case: Nova Capital holds a ₹10 crore equity portfolio with beta 1.2. Nifty futures trade at 25,000 with a lot size of 75. It also writes a call with strike ₹500 on a share now at ₹480, receiving ₹15 premium. At expiry the share is ₹530.

mcqs.q: Value of one Nifty futures contract (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: 25,000 × 75 = ₹18.75 lakh. In practice: lot size changes over time.
mcqs.topic: Forwards and futures: features and pricing

mcqs.q: Contracts to sell to hedge fully (nearest whole):
mcqs.explain: 10 crore × 1.2 ÷ 18.75 lakh = 64. In practice: beta-adjusted hedge.
mcqs.topic: Forwards and futures: features and pricing

mcqs.q: Net result for the call writer per share (₹):
mcqs.explain: Pays 30 (530 − 500), keeps 15 premium. In practice: unlimited upside risk.

mcqs.q: The call writer's break-even share price (₹):
mcqs.explain: Strike + premium. In practice: above it, losses.
